and what was measured.

- round 2: Split layout guide for desktop controls on finish screen [finish, redesign]: predicted +3.0%, measured +0.3% ± 3.8%, after noise correction +0.1%, lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop status hint on waiting screen [home, wait_info]: predicted +1.5%, measured +0.1% ± 2.1%, after noise correction +0.1%, lost: no clear effect

By kind of change, after noise correction:
- adoption, redesign: +9.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, redesign: +0.1% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: +0.9% after noise correction, 2 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: -0.1% after noise correction, 2 test(s)

One test is weak evidence. State a rule only when at least 2 tests of that kind agree after noise correction; otherwise say the evidence is still thin.

Evidence for sign_in, reorder changes is still thin with only one test conducted.
Evidence for home, wait_info changes is still thin with only one test conducted.
Predictions have been consistently too high compared to measured and noise-corrected results.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}
